why:
RFC-0041 / phase 239.1 -- a service client whose REPLY is delivered to a callback the executor dispatches at `spin_once`, rather than awaited. rclrs has one constructor, `NodeState::create_client`, and expresses the delivery mode as an async call on the client it returns; we have no async runtime to await a future on and no allocator to box one with, so the two modes are two CONSTRUCTORS -- `create_client` hands back a `Promise` the caller polls, this one hands back a send handle and takes the callback at creation. Dual-mode by construction, not by preference: the callback is bound at creation for the same reason every other callback in this lane is, which is that the executor's dispatch arena is sized at build time.

On `nros::Node`, the executor-borrowing node handle (`exec.node_mut(id)`); it was `NodeCtx` until phase-483 W2, which the correlator folded onto `Node` (`TYPE_SYNONYMS`). MEASURABLE ONLY SINCE 2026-09-12: `nros_node::executor`'s `mod node` kept the type private while `Executor::node_mut` returned it, so every method on it was callable and none of them had ever produced a row -- issue 1351.
